verified_title: Oxidative Stress-induced Hormonal Disruption in Male Reproduction
abstract: Research into the impacts of oxidative stress (OS), and hormonal balance on reproductive potential has increased over the last 40 years possibly due to rising male infertility. Decreased antioxidant levels and increased OS in tissues result from hormonal imbalance, which in turn leads to male infertility. Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in seminal plasma has been linked to many lifestyle factors such as alcohol and tobacco use, toxicant exposure, obesity, varicocele, stress, and aging. tldr: An overview of the crosslink between OS and gonadal hormone disruption is provided, as well as a potential mode of action in male infertility, to affect key hormonal regulators of male reproductive activities.
